items.headline: Draft Rules under the four Labour Codes released for comments
items.text: The Labour Ministry released draft Rules under the Code on Wages, 2019, Industrial Relations Code, 2020, Code on Social Security, 2020 and OSH Code, 2020. Proposals include a 48-hour weekly cap and social security eligibility for gig workers after 90 days with one aggregator.

items.headline: Winter Session 2025 ends: seven Bills passed, two sent to committees
items.text: Parliament's Winter Session ran from December 1 to 19, 2025. Nine Bills were introduced, seven were passed, and two - the Securities Markets Code, 2025 and the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 - were referred to committees.

items.headline: Parliament passes SHANTI Bill replacing Atomic Energy Act and nuclear liability law
items.text: The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Bill, 2025 replaces the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010. It allows licensing of Indian private companies, sets tiered operator liability of Rs 100-3,000 crore, and gives the AERB statutory status.
items.why: Opens nuclear power to private players and rewrites the liability regime.

items.headline: Parliament passes VB-G RAM G Bill to replace MGNREGA, raising guarantee to 125 days
items.text: The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Bill, 2025 replaces the MGNREGA framework and raises guaranteed work from 100 to 125 days. Costs are shared 60:40 between Centre and states, and states may pause work for up to 60 days.

items.headline: Insurance laws Bill passed, allowing 100% FDI in Indian insurers
items.text: Parliament passed the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, 2025. It raises the FDI cap in Indian insurance companies from 74% to 100%, cuts net-owned fund requirements for foreign reinsurers, and gives IRDAI added powers.

items.headline: Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025 passed, repealing 71 obsolete laws
items.text: Parliament passed the Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025, which repeals 71 obsolete or redundant laws and amends four Acts. Among the changes, the Indian Succession Act, 1925 is amended to remove the need for court validation of wills in certain cases.

items.headline: Securities Markets Code, 2025 introduced and referred to Standing Committee on Finance
items.text: The Securities Markets Code, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha to consolidate the SEBI Act, 1992, the Depositories Act, 1996 and the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956. It was referred to the Standing Committee on Finance.

items.headline: Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 referred to Joint Parliamentary Committee
items.text: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 proposes a single higher education regulator replacing UGC, AICTE and NCTE. After introduction it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

items.headline: Great Indian Bustard: priority areas and undergrounding of power lines (M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India)
items.text: In M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 838/2019) the Supreme Court balanced conservation of the Great Indian Bustard with renewable-energy needs, fixing priority areas and directing critical power lines to be laid underground within two years.

items.headline: Select Committee reports on Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025
items.text: The Select Committee on the IBC (Amendment) Bill, 2025 presented its report. It recommended that a resolution professional be ineligible to act as liquidator in the same case and that the voting threshold for pre-packaged insolvency be cut to 51%.

items.headline: Directions to enforce dowry laws (State of U.P. v. Ajmal Beg)
items.text: In State of U.P. v. Ajmal Beg (Crl.A. No. 132-133/2017) the Supreme Court restored a dowry-death conviction and issued directions on education, training of officers and speedy disposal of dowry cases.

items.headline: Draft amendments to MMDR Act, 1957 propose 50-year leases and coal gasification as mining
items.text: The Ministry of Coal invited comments on draft amendments to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. Proposals include 50-year terms for future leases, allowing sale of legacy mineral stocks, and adding coal gasification to the definition of mining.

items.headline: ICCs can hear complaints across departments (Dr. Sohail Malik v. Union of India)
items.text: In Dr. Sohail Malik v. Union of India (C.A. No. 404/2024) the Supreme Court clarified that an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act can inquire into a complaint even where the respondent works in a different department.

items.body: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
items.headline: DPIIT working paper proposes mandatory blanket licence for AI training on copyrighted works
items.text: DPIIT invited comments on a working paper on generative AI and copyright. It proposes a hybrid model in which AI systems may train on any lawfully accessed work but must pay through a mandatory blanket licence, with creators given a statutory remuneration right.
items.why: A key policy marker on AI training and copyright in India.

items.headline: Winter Session 2025 to run December 1-19 with major Bills listed
items.text: Parliament's Winter Session was scheduled for December 1-19, 2025 (15 sittings). Bills listed for introduction included the Securities Markets Code Bill, Insurance Laws (Amendment) Bill, Higher Education Commission of India Bill, Atomic Energy Bill, a Constitution amendment on Chandigarh and a Bill to repeal about 120 obsolete laws.

items.headline: Draft Post Office Act amendments propose DHRUVA digital addressing system
items.text: The Department of Posts released draft amendments to the Post Office Act, 2023. They provide for a Digital Addressing System (DHRUVA) run through a Network Administrator appointed by the Centre, with civil penalties of up to Rs 1 crore.

items.headline: Draft oil mines safety regulations issued under OSH Code, 2020
items.text: The Labour Ministry invited comments, until January 10, 2026, on draft regulations on occupational safety, health and working conditions in oil mines. They are framed under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020.

items.headline: Four Labour Codes brought into force, replacing 29 labour laws
items.text: The Labour Ministry notified the Code on Wages, 2019, Industrial Relations Code, 2020, Code on Social Security, 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 into effect. They replace 29 laws including the Factories Act, 1948, Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.
items.why: The biggest overhaul of Indian labour law in decades is now operative.

items.headline: Supreme Court answers 16th Presidential Reference on assent to Bills by Governors and President
items.text: A five-judge Supreme Court bench gave its opinion on the 16th Presidential Reference of May 2025, which raised 14 questions on assent to Bills under Article 200 and related provisions. The Court said the judiciary cannot prescribe timelines for grant of assent.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes down provisions of Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021
items.text: In Madras Bar Association v. Union of India, the Supreme Court struck down provisions of the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021 on eligibility, appointment process and tenure of tribunal members. It directed the setting up of a National Tribunals Commission.

items.headline: SC review ruling allows retrospective environmental clearance in exceptional cases
items.text: In Confederation of Real Estate Developers of India v Vanashakti, a review of its earlier ruling, the Supreme Court held that the Environment Protection Act, 1986 does not bar retrospective Environmental Clearance in exceptional circumstances. It validated the 2017 notification for violations pre-dating March 14, 2017.

items.body: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
items.headline: DPIIT invites comments on draft guidelines for use of Geographical Indication logo
items.text: DPIIT invited comments, until December 18, 2025, on draft guidelines for use of the GI logo. The guidelines relate to the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 notified
items.text: MeitY notified the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The Rules set out obligations of data fiduciaries and provide for constitution of the Data Protection Board.

items.headline: RBI notifies trade relief measures for exporters
items.text: The RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Trade Relief Measures) Directions, 2025, alongside amendments to the Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015 notified on November 13. Export proceeds realisation timelines were extended from nine to fifteen months, and eligible exporters got a moratorium on loan repayments and longer credit periods.

items.headline: Written grounds of arrest mandatory for all offences (Mihir Rajesh Shah v. State of Maharashtra)
items.text: In Mihir Rajesh Shah v. State of Maharashtra (Crl.A. No. 2195/2025) the Supreme Court held that grounds of arrest must be given in writing for every offence, at the latest two hours before the accused is produced before the Magistrate.

items.headline: Investigators cannot summon advocates over client advice (In Re: Summoning Advocates)
items.text: In its suo motu case In Re: Summoning Advocates During Investigation (SMW(Crl) No. 2/2025) the Supreme Court restrained investigating agencies from directly summoning counsel about client matters except within the exceptions to legal privilege, and held that in-house counsel do not enjoy the same protection.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI consults on amendments to SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996
items.text: SEBI released a consultation paper proposing amendments to the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996. The proposals concern expense ratios and the management of non-pooled funds.

items.headline: Cabinet approves terms of reference of Eighth Central Pay Commission
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved the terms of reference of the Eighth Central Pay Commission. The Commission will recommend changes to salaries and service conditions of central government employees.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: National Road Safety Board Rules, 2025 notified under Motor Vehicles Act
items.text: MoRTH issued the National Road Safety Board Rules, 2025 under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. The Rules set out the composition and procedures of the Board, which advises on road safety standards.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: IT Rules amended to tighten procedure for content takedown orders
items.text: MeitY notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2025, amending the IT Rules, 2021. Content removal orders to intermediaries now require authorisation at a senior level, must be reasoned, and are subject to periodic review.
items.why: Changes the procedure behind government blocking/takedown directions to platforms.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: Draft IT Rules amendment proposes labelling of synthetically generated (AI) content
items.text: MeitY invited comments on draft Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2025. The draft would require labelling of synthetically generated information and user declarations about such content on platforms.
items.why: First proposed rule-level regime for deepfakes and AI-generated content.

items.headline: Mineral (Auction) Second Amendment Rules, 2025 fix interim timelines for mining leases
items.text: The Ministry of Mines amended the Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015, framed under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. Intermediate deadlines were set for mining plan approval (6 months), environment clearance (18 months) and lease execution (12 months).

items.body: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
items.headline: Draft Rules under National Sports Governance Act, 2025 put out for feedback
items.text: The Sports Ministry released three sets of draft Rules under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025. They cover the composition of the National Sports Board, elections to National Sports Bodies, and appointments to the National Sports Tribunal.

items.headline: Draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2025 released for public comments
items.text: The Ministry of Power invited comments on the draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2025, which seeks to amend the Electricity Act, 2003. Proposals include network sharing among distribution licensees, cost-reflective tariffs, removal of cross-subsidies and a new Electricity Council.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 issued under Environment (Protection) Act
items.text: MoEFCC issued the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target (GEI) Rules, 2025 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The Rules set emission intensity targets for industries including aluminium, cement, chemical processing, and pulp and paper.

items.headline: Draft National Labour and Employment Policy (Shram Shakti Niti 2025) released
items.text: The Labour Ministry released the draft National Labour and Employment Policy, Shram Shakti Niti 2025, for public consultation. It proposes universal social security, better occupational safety and higher female workforce participation.

items.headline: Guidelines to clear cheque-bounce backlog (Sanjabij Tari v. Kishore S. Borcar)
items.text: In Sanjabij Tari v. Kishore S. Borcar (Crl.A. No. 1755/2010) the Supreme Court set out a graded scheme for compounding cheque-dishonour offences and guidelines for faster disposal of Negotiable Instruments Act cases.

items.body: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
items.headline: Draft Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2025 to replace 1959 Act
items.text: MoSPI invited comments until October 24, 2025 on the draft Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2025, which would replace the Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959. It proposes a 12-member Board of Governance responsible for the institute's academic, administrative and technical functions.

items.headline: Seven draft rules under the OSH Code, 2020 released for comments
items.text: The Ministry of Labour and Employment released seven draft rules under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, setting out employer duties for worker safety in docks, mines, motor transport, plantations, beedi, construction and factories. Comments were invited until November 6, 2025.

items.headline: Draft Civil Drone (Promotion and Regulation) Bill, 2025 released for feedback
items.text: The Ministry of Civil Aviation released the draft Civil Drone (Promotion and Regulation) Bill, 2025. It requires registration of unmanned aircraft systems with the DGCA, divides airspace into red, yellow and green zones, and makes operations subject to clearances and third-party insurance.

items.headline: Supreme Court stays certain provisions of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
items.text: A two-judge bench of the Supreme Court passed an interim order staying certain provisions of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, including those on proof of practising Islam and on determining whether property is government property. It directed that the Central Waqf Council have no more than four and State Waqf Boards no more than three non-Muslim members.
items.why: Interim relief in the constitutional challenge to the 2025 Waqf amendments.

items.headline: SEBI eases minimum public offer norms and revises related party transaction thresholds
items.text: SEBI's board approved changes to the minimum public offer and minimum public shareholding requirements under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957, and revised thresholds for material related party transactions under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. It also approved the SWAGAT-FI single-window framework for trusted foreign investors.

items.headline: Draft Telecommunications (User Identification) Rules, 2025 propose biometric SIM verification
items.text: The Department of Telecommunications invited comments until October 19, 2025 on the draft Telecommunications (User Identification) Rules, 2025. The draft requires biometric verification of new users, a shared biometric verification system across telecom entities, and limits SIM transfers to blood relatives or legal heirs.

items.headline: Lawful interception rules amended to let Union Home Secretary act on State requests
items.text: The Telecommunications (Procedures and Safeguards for Lawful Interception of Messages) Amendment Rules, 2025 were notified, amending the 2024 Rules. The Union Home Secretary may now issue interception orders on State government requests that go beyond the State's territorial jurisdiction, and agencies need one or more nodal officers instead of two.

items.headline: 56th GST Council meeting approves two-slab rate structure
items.text: The 56th meeting of the GST Council approved rationalisation of GST into two main slabs of 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate for demerit goods, and cut rates on several essential goods and services. It also approved measures to ease compliance and noted that the GST Appellate Tribunal was to be operationalised by the end of September.

items.headline: TET made mandatory for teachers; minority-school question referred (Anjuman Ishaat E Taleem Trust)
items.text: In Anjuman Ishaat E Taleem Trust v. State of Maharashtra (C.A. No. 1385/2025) the Supreme Court held the Teacher Eligibility Test mandatory for teachers and referred the question of the RTE Act's application to minority institutions to a larger bench.

items.headline: Monsoon Session ends: 14 Bills passed, 13 introduced, 5 referred to committees
items.text: The Monsoon Session of Parliament (July 21 to August 21, 2025) had 21 sittings; 13 Bills were introduced and 14 passed. Bills passed include the Income-Tax (No.2) Bill, 2025, the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025, the Merchant Shipping Bill, 2024 and the Indian Ports Bill, 2025.

items.headline: Parliament passes Income-Tax (No.2) Bill, 2025 to replace the Income-tax Act, 1961
items.text: Parliament passed the Income-Tax (No.2) Bill, 2025 during the Monsoon Session. It replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961 with simplified language and provides for access to 'virtual digital space' during searches.
items.why: Replaces India's six-decade-old income tax statute.

items.headline: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025 passed, banning online money games
items.text: Parliament passed the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025 during the Monsoon Session. It prohibits online money games while promoting e-sports and online social games that involve no stakes.

items.headline: Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 introduced on removal of detained ministers
items.text: The Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 was introduced during the Monsoon Session. It provides for removal of the Prime Minister, a Chief Minister or a Minister detained for 30 consecutive days on charges of offences punishable with five years or more of imprisonment.

items.headline: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025 introduced
items.text: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025 was introduced during the Monsoon Session. It proposes a creditor-initiated insolvency resolution process for corporate debtors and provisions on group insolvency.

items.headline: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025 introduced to decriminalise offences in 17 Acts
items.text: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025 was introduced during the Monsoon Session. It decriminalises or rationalises offences under 17 central Acts and provides for warnings for first-time violations.

items.headline: Merchant Shipping, Coastal Shipping, Indian Ports and Carriage of Goods by Sea Bills passed
items.text: Parliament passed the Merchant Shipping Bill, 2024 (replacing the 1958 Act), the Coastal Shipping Bill, 2024, the Indian Ports Bill, 2025 and the Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2024 (replacing the 1925 Act) during the Monsoon Session.

items.headline: National Sports Governance Bill and National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill passed
items.text: Parliament passed the National Sports Governance Bill, 2025, which sets up a National Sports Board and National Sports Tribunal, and the National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill, 2025 during the Monsoon Session.

items.headline: MMDR Amendment Bill, 2025 passed; Goa Assembly ST seat readjustment Bill also cleared
items.text: Parliament passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2025, allowing inclusion of other minerals in a mining lease, and the Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Bill, 2024.

items.body: Parliament / Standing Committee on Home Affairs
items.headline: Home Affairs panel recommends comprehensive cybercrime law
items.text: The Standing Committee on Home Affairs submitted its report on cybercrime, recommending comprehensive cybercrime legislation, watermarking of AI-generated content and State Cybercrime Coordination Centres.

items.headline: House panel reviews CCI's role, suggests refining Digital Competition Bill thresholds
items.text: A parliamentary Standing Committee reported on the evolving role of the Competition Commission of India, recommending refinement of thresholds under the proposed Digital Competition Bill and more CCI expertise in emerging technologies.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Remediation of Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 notified under Environment (Protection) Act
items.text: The Remediation of Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, laying down procedures for identifying and remediating sites contaminated with hazardous substances.

items.headline: National Sports Governance Bill, 2025 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The National Sports Governance Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha. It provides for a National Sports Board and a National Sports Tribunal to regulate governance of sports bodies.

items.headline: National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill, 2025 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha. It shifts the power to constitute the anti-doping appeal panel from NADA to the central government.

items.headline: Monsoon Session of Parliament begins; 21 sittings planned till August 21
items.text: The Monsoon Session of Parliament commenced on July 21, 2025, with 21 sittings scheduled until August 21, 2025.

items.headline: Select Committee on Income-Tax Bill, 2025 presents its report
items.text: The Select Committee on the Income-Tax Bill, 2025 presented its report, recommending amendments to fix drafting issues and to align certain provisions with the Income-tax Act, 1961.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Environment (Protection) Fourth Amendment Rules, 2025 revise SO2 norms deadlines for thermal plants
items.text: The Environment (Protection) Fourth Amendment Rules, 2025 were notified, modifying the compliance deadlines for sulphur dioxide emission standards applicable to thermal power plants.

items.headline: Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Rules, 2025 notified
items.text: The Ministry of Minority Affairs notified the Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency, and Development Rules, 2025, providing for a registration portal and database of waqf properties.

items.headline: RBI bars pre-payment charges on floating rate loans to individuals and MSMEs
items.text: The RBI issued directions prohibiting pre-payment charges on floating rate loans taken by individuals and MSMEs, effective January 1, 2026.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Hazardous Waste Rules amended to bring non-ferrous metal scrap under EPR
items.text: The Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Amendment Rules, 2025 were notified, regulating recycling of non-ferrous metal scrap through extended producer responsibility.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: Motor Vehicle Aggregators Guidelines, 2025 replace 2020 guidelines
items.text: The Motor Vehicle Aggregators Guidelines, 2025 were released, replacing the 2020 guidelines. Changes include reduced suspension periods and a requirement for psychological assessment of drivers.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Model Rules for Felling of Trees in Agricultural Land, 2025 released
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the Model Rules for Felling of Trees in Agricultural Land, 2025, setting out registration and permit procedures for felling trees grown under agroforestry.

items.headline: Draft Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Amendment Rules, 2025 put out for comment
items.text: The Department of Telecommunications invited comments on the draft Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Amendment Rules, 2025, dealing with collection of data relating to users of telecommunication identifiers.

items.headline: RBI cuts priority sector lending target for small finance banks to 60%
items.text: The RBI reduced the priority sector lending requirement for small finance banks from 75% to 60% of adjusted net bank credit or credit equivalent of off-balance sheet exposures.

items.headline: RBI issues Project Finance Directions, 2025, effective October 1, 2025
items.text: The RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Project Finance) Directions, 2025, setting conditions for lending by regulated entities to projects. The directions take effect from October 1, 2025.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI board approves changes to merchant banker and debenture trustee rules
items.text: At its board meeting, SEBI approved changes to the regulations governing merchant bankers and debenture trustees, a lower minimum lot size for Infrastructure Investment Trusts, and verification requirements for investors in angel funds.

items.headline: CERC proposes Power Markets (First Amendment) Regulations, 2025
items.text: CERC invited comments on the draft CERC (Power Markets) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2025, expanding over-the-counter contracts to cover capacity contracts, renewable energy certificates, virtual power purchase agreements and battery storage contracts.

items.headline: Draft Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2025 would let consumers own energy storage systems
items.text: The Ministry of Power invited comments on the draft Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2025, which would allow end-use consumers to develop, own, lease or operate energy storage systems, beyond generating companies and transmission and distribution licensees.

items.headline: RBI issues Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025
items.text: The RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025, laying down loan-to-value ratios and credit appraisal requirements for loans backed by gold and silver.

items.headline: Census-2027 to be held in two phases with caste enumeration; reference date March 1, 2027
items.text: The government announced that Population Census-2027 will be conducted in two phases along with enumeration of castes. The reference date is March 1, 2027, and October 1, 2026 for Ladakh and snow-bound areas.

items.headline: SEZ Rules, 2006 amended to ease land norms for semiconductor and electronics SEZs
items.text: The Commerce Ministry notified amendments to the Special Economic Zones Rules, 2006, reducing the minimum land area required for SEZs for semiconductor and electronic component manufacturing to 10 hectares.

items.headline: Draft Registration Bill, 2025 released to replace the Registration Act, 1908
items.text: The Ministry of Rural Development released the draft Registration Bill, 2025 for public comments, proposing to repeal the Registration Act, 1908. The draft expands the list of documents requiring compulsory registration and enables electronic submission of documents; comments were invited until June 25, 2025.
items.why: Would overhaul the 117-year-old law on registration of property documents.

items.headline: Maternity leave allowed for child from second marriage (K. Umadevi v. Government of Tamil Nadu)
items.text: In K. Umadevi v. Government of Tamil Nadu (C.A. No. 2526/2025) the Supreme Court held that a woman employee is entitled to maternity leave for a child from a subsequent marriage, even if she has children from an earlier marriage.

items.headline: CERC invites comments on draft guidelines for virtual power purchase agreements
items.text: CERC invited comments on draft guidelines for virtual power purchase agreements, which would let designated consumers meet renewable energy obligations through financial contracts with renewable generators.

items.headline: RBI notifies Payments Regulatory Board Regulations, 2025
items.text: The RBI notified the Payments Regulatory Board Regulations, 2025, repealing the Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems Regulations, 2008. The regulations restructure the Board's composition, including government-nominated members with payments and technology expertise.

items.headline: Three-year practice rule restored for Civil Judge entry (All India Judges Association v. Union of India)
items.text: In All India Judges Association v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 1022/1989) the Supreme Court restored the requirement of three years' practice for entry-level judicial service, restored the 25% LDCE quota for promotion to District Judge and set related promotion criteria.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes down retrospective environmental clearances in Vanashakti v Union of India
items.text: In Vanashakti v Union of India, the Supreme Court held that grant of retrospective (ex post facto) environmental clearances is contrary to environmental law and the EIA Notification, and struck down the 2017 notification that permitted such clearances.

items.headline: TRAI recommends pricing of spectrum for satellite communication
items.text: TRAI released recommendations on spectrum for satellite-based communication services, proposing spectrum charges linked to 4% of adjusted gross revenue or an annual fee of Rs 3,500 per MHz.

items.headline: RBI removes limits on FPI investment in corporate debt securities
items.text: The RBI removed the investment limit applicable to foreign portfolio investors investing in corporate debt securities, with the stated aim of easing investment.

items.headline: Cabinet approves revised SHAKTI policy for coal allocation to power sector
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved a revised SHAKTI policy for allocation of coal to the power sector. Private generators may obtain coal linkages for up to 12 months or for between one and 25 years, with more flexibility in selling electricity.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025 notified
items.text: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways notified the Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025. Road accident victims are entitled to cashless treatment at designated hospitals up to Rs 1.5 lakh per victim, for up to seven days from the accident.

items.headline: Ministry of Mines releases draft amendments to mineral auction rules
items.text: The Ministry of Mines released draft amendments to the mineral auction rules for comments. The draft introduces intermediate timelines for steps such as execution of mining leases and obtaining environmental clearances.

items.headline: Union Cabinet approves caste enumeration in the next Census
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved the inclusion of caste enumeration in the upcoming population census.

items.headline: TRAI recommends framework for critical machine-to-machine services
items.text: TRAI released recommendations on designating critical services in machine-to-machine (M2M) communication, proposing technology-agnostic criteria for classifying such services and a framework for transfer of M2M service authorisations.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 issued for comments
items.text: The Environment Ministry issued the draft Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025. The draft specifies emission intensity targets for obligated entities under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023.

items.headline: Finance Ministry notifies amalgamation of 26 Regional Rural Banks
items.text: The Ministry of Finance notified the amalgamation of 26 Regional Rural Banks across 10 states and one union territory, following the 'One State, One RRB' principle.

items.headline: Budget Session 2025 of Parliament concludes with ten Bills passed
items.text: The Budget Session of Parliament, held from January 31 to April 4, 2025, concluded with ten Bills passed. These included the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025 and the Boilers Bill, 2024.

items.headline: Parliament passes Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 amending the Waqf Act, 1995
items.text: Parliament passed the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 during the Budget Session. It amends the Waqf Act, 1995 to permit creation of waqf only by persons practising Islam for at least five years, removes the concept of waqf by user, and provides for non-Muslim members on waqf boards.
items.why: Significantly changes the legal framework for creation and administration of waqf properties.

items.headline: Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025 passed, consolidating four immigration laws
items.text: Parliament passed the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025 during the Budget Session. The Bill consolidates four Acts governing the entry, stay and registration of foreigners and immigration into India into a single law.

items.headline: Parliament passes Protection of Interests in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025
items.text: Parliament passed the Protection of Interests in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025 during the Budget Session. The Bill gives effect in India to the Cape Town Convention, 2001 and its Aircraft Protocol on international interests in mobile equipment, relevant to aircraft leasing and financing.

items.headline: Tribhuvan Sahkari University Bill, 2025 passed by Parliament
items.text: Parliament passed the Tribhuvan Sahkari University Bill, 2025, which establishes the Institute of Rural Management Anand, Gujarat as the Tribhuvan Sahkari University, a university for the cooperative sector, while retaining the institute's autonomous character.

items.body: Parliament / Standing Committee on External Affairs
items.headline: House panel reports on diaspora welfare and pending Emigration Bill, 2024
items.text: The Standing Committee on External Affairs presented its report on the welfare of the Indian diaspora and the status of the Emigration Bill, 2024. It recommended a comprehensive diaspora policy and that legislative action on the Emigration Bill be prioritised.

items.headline: Indian Ports Bill, 2025 introduced to replace the Indian Ports Act, 1908
items.text: The Indian Ports Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha to replace the Indian Ports Act, 1908. It establishes a Maritime State Development Council and provides for dispute resolution committees.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI board raises FPI disclosure threshold and sets up conflict-of-interest review panel
items.text: At its board meeting, SEBI raised the threshold for additional FPI disclosures from Rs 25,000 crore to Rs 50,000 crore, allowed investment advisers to collect fees in advance for up to one year, and constituted a high-level committee to review conflict-of-interest rules.

items.headline: RBI issues revised priority sector lending directions
items.text: The RBI revised its priority sector lending directions, fixing the target for urban cooperative banks at 60%, raising the renewable energy loan limit to Rs 35 crore, and adding transgender persons and joint liability groups to the weaker sections category.

items.headline: Centre notifies revised investment and turnover thresholds for classifying MSMEs
items.text: The Ministry of MSME revised the classification thresholds with effect from April 1, 2025: micro (investment Rs 2.5 crore, turnover Rs 10 crore), small (Rs 25 crore, Rs 100 crore) and medium (Rs 125 crore, Rs 500 crore).

items.headline: Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha and was subsequently passed by the House. It repeals four earlier laws, mandates registration of foreigners on arrival, and requires educational and medical institutions to furnish prescribed information about foreigners.

items.headline: Budget Session resumes after recess
items.text: The second half of the Budget Session of Parliament began on March 10, 2025 and was scheduled to end on April 4, 2025.

items.headline: RBI proposes ban on foreclosure charges for floating-rate business loans to individuals and MSEs
items.text: The RBI issued a draft circular on responsible lending conduct proposing that regulated entities must not levy foreclosure charges or pre-payment penalties on floating-rate business loans to individuals and micro and small enterprises, up to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 7.5 crore. Comments were invited until March 21, 2025.

items.headline: Income-Tax Bill, 2025 introduced to replace the Income-Tax Act, 1961
items.text: The Income-Tax Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha and referred to a Select Committee. It seeks to replace the Income-Tax Act, 1961 while retaining most of its existing provisions.

items.headline: First half of Budget Session concludes; second half from March 10
items.text: The first half of the Budget Session ran from January 31 to February 13, 2025. The second half was scheduled from March 10 to April 4, 2025.

items.headline: Protection of Interests in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025 introduced in Rajya Sabha
items.text: The Protection of Interests in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025 was introduced in Rajya Sabha to give legal effect to international conventions that secure creditors' rights over aircraft and related assets on default.

items.headline: Tribhuvan Sahkari University Bill, 2025 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The 'Tribhuvan' Sahkari University Bill, 2025 was introduced in Lok Sabha to establish the Institute of Rural Management Anand as a university for education and training in the cooperative sector.

items.headline: Union Budget 2025-26 presented in Lok Sabha
items.text: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2025-26, with total expenditure of Rs 50,65,345 crore and a fiscal deficit target of 4.4% of GDP. Tax proposals included a full rebate for annual income up to Rs 12 lakh under the new regime and higher TDS/TCS thresholds.

items.headline: Budget Session 2025 begins with President's address to joint sitting
items.text: Parliament's Budget Session commenced on January 31, 2025 with 27 sittings scheduled up to April 4, 2025. President Droupadi Murmu addressed a joint sitting of both Houses the same day, and the Economic Survey 2024-25 was tabled.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules amended to widen permitted purposes
items.text: MeitY notified amendments to the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance (Social Welfare, Innovation, Knowledge) Rules, 2020, expanding the purposes for which Aadhaar authentication may be permitted.

items.headline: JPC submits report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024
items.text: The Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 submitted its report. Among other things, it recommended that the removal of 'waqf by user' apply only prospectively.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes down domicile-based reservation in PG medical admissions
items.text: A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that residence-based reservation in admissions to postgraduate medical courses violates the right to equality under Article 14 of the Constitution.

items.headline: Draft Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2025 released
items.text: The Department of Consumer Affairs released the draft Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2025, which would mandate Indian Standard Time as the official time reference for commercial and administrative activities.

items.headline: SEBI consults on widening the social stock exchange framework
items.text: SEBI issued a consultation paper reviewing the framework for the social stock exchange. It proposed expanding the types of non-profit organisations and social enterprises eligible to register and raise funds on the platform, with comments invited until February 10, 2025.

items.headline: Cable Television Network Rules amended to move cable operator registration online
items.text: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting amended the Cable Television Network Rules, 1994, shifting registration of local cable operators from post offices to an online system administered by the Ministry.

items.headline: UGC issues draft 2025 Regulations on appointment of teachers and Vice-Chancellors
items.text: The UGC issued the draft UGC (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment and Promotion of Teachers and Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education) Regulations, 2025, covering faculty and Vice-Chancellor appointments. Comments were due by February 5, 2025.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: Draft Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 released for comments
items.text: MeitY published the draft Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The draft covers obligations of data fiduciaries, verifiable parental consent for processing children's data, intimation of personal data breaches, and the functioning of the Data Protection Board; comments were invited until February 18, 2025.
items.why: First draft of the rules needed to operationalise India's data protection law.
